DeBlassie gave a probabilistic proof on bounded Lipschitz domains for s = 1/m with
integers m > 2 [3, Theorem 1.1]. These arguments therefore apply to a discrete family of
exponents. Abatangelo and Jarohs proved (1.2) for s ∈ (1/2, 1) by a computer-assisted
analysis of explicit potentials [1]. Their method also gives superharmonicity in balls for
s ∈ (1/2, 1) in dimensions 2 ≤ n ≤ 11. It relies on delicate estimates of the available
potentials for the fractional Laplacian in balls; see also [11]. Both the restriction on s and
the dimensional threshold enter through the estimates of the corresponding kernels.
   Our main result, Theorem 1.1, settles (1.2). In fact, whenever a non-negative eigenfunc-
tion exists, it is strictly superharmonic, with a quantitative pointwise lower bound, on an
arbitrary open set throughout the full range s ∈ (0, 1).
